Photograph: Dylan Martinez/Reuters Niall McVeigh Sat 31 Oct 2026 14.30 EDT First published on Sat 31 Oct 2026 12.30 EDT Share Key events 12m ago Half time: Tottenham 1-0 Crystal Palace 
 34m ago GOAL! Tottenham 1-0 Crystal Palace (Gray 24') 
 44m ago Red card! Mateta is sent off for Palace 
 1h ago Here we go 
 2h ago Team news 
 2h ago Preamble 
 33s ago 14.30 EDT “Re: Mateta. If a player decides to slide in, uncontrolled from behind, with their studs up … c’mon, we’ve all got work in the morning,” writes David Penney.
 Share 12m ago 14.19 EDT Half time: Tottenham 1-0 Crystal Palace
 Spurs end the first half a goal and a man up thanks to Archie Gray’s header, after Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off following a VAR review. The hosts have dominated, but need another goal or two to avoid any second-half nerves.
 Share 14m ago 14.17 EDT 46 mins: Unfortunately, Dwight McNeil’s through ball lands harmlessly in the giant, Jean-Philippe Mateta-shaped hole in the Tottenham half.
 Share 15m ago 14.16 EDT 45 mins: Two added minutes, and another Spurs free kick to fend off for Palace. Fernandes’ cross is cleared at the far post, and Palace try to break …
 Share 16m ago 14.15 EDT 43 mins: Half-hearted shouts for a penalty from the Spurs fans as Mingueza grapples with Tel in the Palace area. Nothing doing from the referee or VAR.
 Share 18m ago 14.13 EDT 42 mins: Marmoush smashes an effort at goal, but only connects with poor Jaydee Canvot’s head, a couple of yards away. Spurs get a corner, but Palace deal with it.
 Share 19m ago 14.12 EDT 40 mins: Andy Robertson has had enough of this tiki-taka muck, and has a crack at goal from 30 yards that’s well-struck, but patted down easily enough by Henderson.
 Share 20m ago 14.11 EDT 37 mins: Anyway, Palace really need to keep this deficit to one at half-time. They’re camping out on the edge of their area, with Spurs taking their time in possession.
 Share 24m ago 14.06 EDT “Everything that’s wrong with VAR in 90 odd seconds: even if that is a red card challenge – spoiler, it’s not and never will be – has Oliver made a clear and obvious error in showing a yellow? The answer, my friend, is no.”
 There seems a consensus that it was harsh, but for me, Mateta dived in and caught Van de Ven’s heel with his studs. Not saying he meant it, but without a VAR intervention, I imagine some people would be saying Palace got away with one.
 Share Updated at  14.09 EDT 27m ago 14.04 EDT 32 mins: Pino turns on the halfway line and is hauled over by Fernandes, who doesn’t need to do anything silly at this stage. Just a free kick, though.
 Share 28m ago 14.02 EDT 30 mins: Kamada tries to carry the ball out of his own half, but he and Adam Wharton are crowded by a clutch of white shirts.
 Share 29m ago 14.02 EDT 28 mins: Spurs fan take a moment to bellow their appreciation for Harry Kane, after his Ballon d’Or success last week.
 Share 32m ago 13.59 EDT 26 mins: Robertson takes a free kick and it’s flicked over the bar by Solanke. Palace are all over the shop defensively. Steve Parish is watching on here, perhaps considering giving Oli Glasner a call.
 Share 34m ago 13.56 EDT GOAL! Tottenham 1-0 Crystal Palace (Gray 24')
 Kudus causes more trouble down the right and wins a corner. He takes it – and whips a terrific cross to Archie Gray, who is given the freedom of North London and nods the ball beyond Henderson!
 View image in fullscreen Tottenham Hotspur’s Archie Gray celebrates scoring their first goal. Photograph: Dylan Martinez/Reuters View image in fullscreen Gray celebrates. Photograph: Dylan Martinez/Reuters Share Updated at  14.10 EDT 36m ago 13.54 EDT 22 mins: Tel is at the heart of Spurs’ creative output so far, and his curling cross from the left side is just beyond Kudus, advancing unmarked at the back post.
 Share 38m ago 13.53 EDT 21 mins: Pino almost twists and turns in on goal, but the flag goes up. Palace going a goal up when they’re already a man down would certainly make things interesting.
 Share 39m ago 13.51 EDT 19 mins: Can Palace pose any threat without their attacking talisman? Oscar Mingueza, who starts here after impressing in the Carabao Cup win at Fulham, gets away down the right flank but his cross is blocked by Tonali.
 Share 41m ago 13.50 EDT 17 mins: Silky skills from Mathys Tel to get in behind down the left, but his cut-back can’t pick out Solanke, or anyone else in a white shirt.
 Share 42m ago 13.48 EDT 15 mins: There are howls from Palace fans as Archie Gray goes in heavily on Kamada – he’s shown a yellow card.
 Share 43m ago 13.47 EDT 14 mins: Robertson’s cross is flicked away by Mitchell, with Kudus waiting to pounce at the far post.
 Share 44m ago 13.46 EDT Red card! Mateta is sent off for Palace
 A booking initially seemed the right call, but the replays don’t look good – and it’s no surprise when Oliver trots back from the monitor and sends Mateta off!
 View image in fullscreen Referee Michael Oliver checks out the monitor. Photograph: Dylan Martinez/Reuters View image in fullscreen Mateta heads off for his early bath. Photograph: Jordan Pettitt/PA Share Updated at  14.18 EDT 45m ago 13.45 EDT 11 mins: Oof! Van de Ven chases back to deny Mateta on the break, and the Palace forward lunges in, his studs catching the defender’s heel. Yellow card shown by Michael Oliver – but VAR wants a word …
 View image in fullscreen Crystal Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta (centre) dives in to tackle Tottenham Hotspur's Micky van de Ven ... Photograph: Jordan Pettitt/PA View image in fullscreen Van de Ven yelps in pain after being fouled by Jean-Philippe Mateta. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters View image in fullscreen Jan Paul van Hecke (centre) lets Mateta know what he thinks of his challenge. Photograph: Jordan Pettitt/PA Share Updated at  14.07 EDT 47m ago 13.43 EDT 9 mins: At the other end, Kamada stings Kinsky’s palms with a shot from the edge of the area.
 Share 49m ago 13.42 EDT 8 mins: Fernandes concedes a free kick after trying and failing to outmuscle Mateta close to the Palace area.
 Share 49m ago 13.41 EDT 6 mins: Spurs enjoying the early possession, stroking the ball swiftly around midfield.
 Share 53m ago 13.37 EDT 3 mins: If Palace can get a point here, then Manchester United will drop into the bottom three. And as long as the visitors are level, United are in there provisionally .
 Share 55m ago 13.36 EDT 2 mins: Palace have the league’s leakiest defence, and are particularly vulnerable in the early stages. Tottenham win an early corner, but nothing comes from it.
 Share 1h ago 13.34 EDT Here we go
 Palace kick off and play back to Henderson, while four players charge forward to try and meet his clearance downfield. It doesn’t work.
 Share 1h ago 13.31 EDT Before we begin, there will be a minute’s silence, plus the Last Post, to mark Remembrance Day.
 Share Updated at  13.32 EDT 1h ago 13.21 EDT This is a north-south London derby, but Google Maps tells me it takes an hour and a half to go from Selhurst Park to here on public transport. Are there any longer away trips to a venue in the same city? Maybe a question for the Knowledge.
 Which footballers have scored in the same minute as their surname? | The Knowledge Read more Share 1h ago 13.17 EDT Here’s Roberto De Zerbi , who leaves James Maddison on the bench – “James is very important for us – when he feels good, he plays” – and starts Dominic Solanke up front. “I think Omar Marmoush can play in behind, he has often played behind another striker,” he adds. “We have to keep the right spirit and mentality – a few days ago, we were last in the table and we must not forget it.”
 Share 1h ago 13.02 EDT Here are today’s Premier League results so far:
 Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United
 Bournemouth 2-0 Leeds
 Brentford 2-0 Nottm Forest
 Coventry 3-1 Sunderland
 Hull City 2-2 Ipswich
 Manchester City 0-1 Brighton
 Manchester City 0-1 Brighton, Coventry 3-1 Sunderland and more: clockwatch - live Read more Share 2h ago 12.46 EDT Team news
 Tottenham Hotspur (4-2-3-1): Kinsky; Gray, van Hecke, van de Ven, Robertson; Fernandes, Tonali; Kudus, Marmoush, Tel; Solanke.
 Subs: Dubravka, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Udogie, Kulusevski, Porro, Davies, Williams-Barnet. 
 Crystal Palace (3-4-2-1): Henderson; Richards, Disasi, Canvot; Mingueza, Wharton, Kamada, Mitchell; McNeil, Pino; Mateta.
 Subs: Benitez, Lerma, Nketiah, Hughes, Osorio, Khalaili, Doucoure, Guessand, Chilwell. 
 Referee: Michael Oliver.
 Share 2h ago 12.30 EDT Preamble
 By recent standards, it’s been a very successful fortnight for Spurs. Two Premier League wins on the bounce have lifted Roberto De Zerbi’s side up the table, and they can now also lay claim to having developed the best men’s footballer in the world .
 Harry Kane usually enjoyed games against Crystal Palace, scoring 11 goals in 20 appearances against the Eagles. Palace have won on their last two visits to the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, though, including a hellish 3-1 defeat in March that left Spurs staring into the abyss .
 Tottenham are seeking a trouble-free victory today as proof that those dark days are finally behind them. Defeat for Palace, meanwhile, could push them closer to the trapdoor and pile pressure on Pierre Sage. Kick-off: 5.30pm GMT.
